claim: A RepE/LAT correctness direction from last-token hidden states outperforms intrinsic likelihood and verbalized (reflective) confidence at picking the correct implementation among four candidates on HumanEval and BigCodeBench for four 7-8B instruct LLMs.
stance_target: L2 probe-beats-verbal on code is occupied
scope_conditions: Four 7-8B Instruct models; candidate-selection accuracy not calibration (Sec 4.2.1)
quoted_support: LAT consistently outperforms all baselines. On BigCodeBench , it improves accuracy by +13.3 to +29.0 pp over the best reflective accuracy; on HumanEval , gains range from +8.7 to +26.2 pp over the strongest baseline.

breadth.confidence_families: Intrinsic length-normalized sequence likelihood; reflective verbalized (Regular 7-level, True/False); hidden-state RepE/LAT reading (Sec 2.3, 3, 4.1.3)
breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present (searched: 'base model' appears once only in background; all four targets are Instruct, Sec 4.1.4)
breadth.post_training_stages: not present (searched: SFT/RLHF/post-training comparison; only instruct checkpoints used)
breadth.reasoning_models: not present (searched: 'reasoning'; five hits, none about reasoning-mode models; reasoning off/not studied)
breadth.elicitation_formats: Verbalized Regular (7 levels, mapped to -1..1, weighted by token probability) and True/False; LAT prompt 'Consider the amount of correctness...' (Sec 2.3, 3, Listing 6)
breadth.benchmarks: HumanEval (QA_HE 151 tasks), BigCodeBench (QA_BCB 457 tasks), MBPP+ and 20 synthetic tasks for OOD fitting (Sec 4.1.1, Tables 1-2)
breadth.label_source: Unit-test execution against benchmark test suites; reference solution assumed correct (Sec 3)
breadth.label_independence: Incorrect candidates come from other LLMs (Llama-3.3-70B, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash for BCB; Llama-3.2-3B, Gemma-3-1B, Granite-3.3-2B for HE) not the probed model, in RQ1; in RQ2 the model ranks its own 10 samples (Sec 4.1.1, 5.1.1)
breadth.contamination_split: not present (searched: contaminat, cutoff, release date, LiveCodeBench: 0 hits); splits are task-level 10-fold CV with 10%/10%/80% Fit/Val/Test (Sec 4.1.2)
breadth.calibration_metrics: Selection accuracy among 4 candidates and pass@rank-k; no ECE/AUROC/Brier of confidence (searched: AUROC 0 hits; calibration only cited as background)
breadth.granularity: Whole solution (pairwise correct vs incorrect; four-way candidate choice); no per-requirement or per-line
breadth.causal_intervention: not present (searched: steer, causal: 0 hits; Sec 6.3 states 'we showed that this signal exists and can be leveraged but not why or how it exists')

claim: Out-of-distribution fitting of the correctness direction is erratic: synthetic fitting drops below random for Qwen (12.2%) and CodeLlama (22.2%) on BigCodeBench, MBPP+ fitting stays above random on HumanEval (32.2%-39.9%) but below in-distribution (41.4-60.7%).
quoted_support: Synthetic fitting is erratic: two models drop below random (Qwen at 12.2%, CodeLlama at 22.2%), while Mistral and OpenCoder exceed it.

claim: Ranking 10 self-samples by LAT lifts pass@rank-1 above pass@1 without test execution; e.g. Mistral HumanEval Fit_HE reaches 41.3% at rank-1 versus 34.7% pass@1 and RankEF 35.5%; the paper reports only a few comparisons were statistically significant.
stance_target: probe-based ranking (selection utility, not budget routing) is occupied at whole-solution level
scope_conditions: Sec 5.2; test execution used only for evaluation
quoted_support: Numerically, LAT shows superior or comparable accuracy to all baselines, including RankEF, across most settings. Only a few comparisons reached statistical significance.
